issues.t: Lower intake manifold gasket leaks coolant or oil
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell, coolant or oil seeping from where the intake meets the engine, overheating, or oil that looks milky on the dipstick.
issues.why: The original intake manifold gaskets on the 3.1L V6 have plastic carriers and soft seals that deform with heat and age. Coolant can leak outside or into the engine oil, often starting around 60,000 miles. It is the worst engine complaint on the Century.
issues.next: Have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and check the oil for coolant as soon as you notice coolant loss. Replace both gaskets with the updated design along with new bolts, and change the oil and coolant. Stop driving if it overheats, since that can crack a cylinder head.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or fails
issues.sym: The engine revs up but the car does not speed up, shifts are delayed or missing, the car feels stuck in one gear, or it will not move in drive or reverse.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic wears internally with age and mileage. CarComplaints rates a slipping transmission on the 2000 Century as its single worst problem, and GM issued many bulletins on slipping, shudder and loss of drive.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell. Get the codes read and a transmission diagnosis early; small problems such as a solenoid can be cheaper to fix before the clutches burn.

issues.t: Harsh or slipping shifts from a pressure control solenoid
issues.sym: Hard, banging upshifts, slipping, and a check engine light, often with codes P1811 or P0748.
issues.why: The pressure control solenoid in the transmission sets how firmly gears engage. GM issued a bulletin to replace this solenoid when it causes harsh or slipping shifts.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A solenoid can often be replaced without removing the transmission. Ask the shop about GM bulletin 02-07-30-048.

issues.t: Transmission drops into neutral at highway speed
issues.sym: While cruising, the transmission suddenly feels like it is in neutral, or it loses drive when shifting out of fourth gear.
issues.why: GM issued a service alert for intermittent loss of drive on these cars. The fix was to replace the transmission valve body.
issues.next: Get off the road safely if drive is lost. Have a shop check for this known valve body problem before replacing the whole transmission.

issues.t: Power window falls down or stops working
issues.sym: The window drops into the door, moves crooked, makes a grinding or snapping noise, or does not move at all.
issues.why: The window regulator cable breaks or comes off its pulley, or the window motor wears out. A dead power window is the single most reported Century complaint.
issues.next: Prop or tape the glass up to keep rain out. A shop can tell whether the regulator, motor or switch is at fault before replacing parts.

issues.t: Power window switch fails
issues.sym: A window works only sometimes, works from one switch but not another, or stops responding completely.
issues.why: The window switches wear out internally. They often work on and off for a while before failing completely.
issues.next: Try the window from the driver's master switch and the door switch to narrow it down. A replacement switch is cheap and easy to fit.

issues.t: Sludge in the coolant leads to overheating
issues.sym: Brown, muddy coolant or crust in the reservoir, weak heat from the vents, or the temperature gauge running higher than normal.
issues.why: Old coolant mixed with oil or air from a leaking intake gasket breaks down into sludge that clogs the radiator and heater core.
issues.next: Have the cooling system and intake gaskets checked. Fix the leak first, then flush the system thoroughly and refill with fresh coolant.

issues.t: Hard starts and rough idle from clogged fuel injectors
issues.sym: Hard starting, chugging, a rough idle and occasional misfires, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: GM issued repeated bulletins on these engines for fuel injectors clogged with deposits, which upset the fuel spray.
issues.next: Try a quality fuel system cleaner and top-tier fuel first. If it continues, a shop can clean or replace the injectors.

issues.t: Knocking or rattling when the engine is cold
issues.sym: A knock, rattle or tap from the engine for the first few minutes after a cold start or under light load, which fades as the engine warms.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for cold-engine knock on these engines. In some cases the fix was replacing pistons, and GM later released coated service pistons.
issues.next: If the noise goes away when warm and oil level and pressure are fine, it is usually not urgent. Have it checked if the noise gets louder or stays when warm.

issues.t: Misfire from a failing ignition coil
issues.sym: A shaking engine, loss of power, a flashing check engine light and misfire codes.
issues.why: The ignition coils and the ignition module under them wear out. Worn spark plugs and wires add strain on the coils.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Replacing the bad coil, and plugs and wires if they are old, usually fixes it. Do not drive far with a flashing check engine light.

issues.t: ABS warning light comes on
issues.sym: The ABS light turns on now and then or stays on. The normal brakes still work, but anti-lock does not.
issues.why: Usually a failing wheel speed sensor or its wiring. GM issued several bulletins on intermittent ABS lights on the Century.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read to find which wheel is at fault. The sensor is usually an inexpensive part.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing growls
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise from the front that gets louder with speed and changes when you turn.
issues.why: The sealed front hub bearing wears out. Owners report replacing them on many Centurys.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked. Replace a noisy one soon, since a failing bearing can get hot and loose.

issues.t: Worn struts, springs and control arms
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, a bouncy or floaty ride, uneven tire wear, or the car sitting lower on one corner.
issues.why: Struts, coil springs and control arm bushings wear out with age. Owners report broken front springs and worn lower control arms.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Replace worn parts in pairs and get an alignment afterward.

issues.t: Rear drum brakes stick or seize
issues.sym: Grinding or scraping from the rear, a hot rear wheel, the car pulling, or a parking brake that does not release fully.
issues.why: The rear drum brake parts and adjusters corrode and stick, especially in salty areas.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes inspected. Shoes, drums and hardware are usually replaced on both sides.

issues.t: Blower fan only works on high
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan works only on the highest setting, or not at all on some speeds.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor burns out. It is a common and cheap part.
issues.next: Replace the blower motor resistor. If the new one fails quickly, have the blower motor checked for drawing too much current.

issues.t: Tilt steering column sticks in the up position
issues.sym: The tilt steering wheel locks in the highest position or another position and will not release.
issues.why: GM issued several bulletins about the tilt column mechanism sticking or binding.
issues.next: Do not force the lever. A dealer or shop can repair the tilt mechanism under the bulletin procedure.

issues.t: Gauges go dead and the car will not crank
issues.sym: The instrument cluster stops working, warning lights come on, and the engine may not crank.
issues.why: GM bulletins trace this to low ignition voltage through the ignition switch or body control module.
issues.next: Have a shop check ignition switch output voltage. A new ignition switch or body control module is the usual fix.

issues.t: Oil pan gasket leak
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine and oily residue on the bottom of the oil pan.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins on repeat oil pan gasket leaks for these engines.
issues.next: Check the oil level often. A shop can clean the area to confirm the leak before replacing the gasket.

issues.t: ABS motor short can cause an underhood fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from under the hood, or a fuel smell.
issues.why: An electrical short in the ABS motor can overheat a nearby brake pipe, which can melt a fuel hose and start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 99V-170. If you smell burning or fuel, stop and turn off the engine.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers quit suddenly, which leaves you unable to see in rain or snow.
issues.why: A defect in the wiper system could cause the wipers to fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 99V-348 and have the dealer do the free repair.

issues.t: Headlights cannot be aimed correctly (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights seem aimed wrong, especially after a headlamp assembly has been replaced.
issues.why: Some replacement headlamp assemblies could not be aimed properly, and a second lighting recall covered other cars that did not meet the federal lighting standard.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 98V-102 and 99V-356.

issues.t: Dim headlight bulbs (recall)
issues.sym: The headlights seem weak, making overhead signs hard to read at night.
issues.why: Some headlamp bulbs gave less light than they should.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 04V-375. The dealer replaces the bulbs.

issues.t: Rear wheel can shift and steer the car (recall)
issues.sym: The car feels unstable or pulls, especially when braking.
issues.why: A problem with the rear drum brake assembly could let a rear wheel shift, causing rear steering and possible loss of control.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 00V-143 and get it inspected right away.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle may not hold in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: There may be no warning signs.
issues.why: Some seat belt buckles from TRW might not restrain a person properly in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 00V-228. The dealer replaces affected buckles for free.

issues.t: Rear seat belt anchors may pull loose (recall)
issues.sym: There may be no warning signs.
issues.why: The rear outboard seat belt anchors might not hold the required load, so a belt could separate from the body in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 95V-173. The dealer installs new anchor bolts.
